Figure 1. Typical plant type III PKSs that use 4-coumaroyl-CoA as the starter unit and malonyl-CoA as the extender unit. (A)

figure_candidates.label: Figure 2
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 2. Reactions catalyzed by OKS. (A) Synthesis of two octaketides SEK4b and SEK4 from eight molecules of malonyl-CoA.
(B) Synthesis of C19 hexaketide stilbene and C21 heptaketide chalcone by OKS from 4-coumaroyl-CoA and malonyl-CoA.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 3
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 3. Biosynthetic pathways of curcuminoids. (A) Biosynthesis of curcuminoids by DCS and CURS. DCS catalyzes the forma-
tion of diketide-CoAs by condensing 4-coumaroyl-CoA or feruloyl-CoA with malonyl-CoA. CURS then condenses the diketide-
CoAs with aromatic CoA starters to form curcuminoids. (B) Biosynthesis of curcuminoids by CUS. CUS ﬁrst synthesizes a dike-
tide-CoA and then uses the b-keto acid which is engendered from the diketide-CoA as the second extender unit to afford curcumi-
noids.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 4
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 4. Representative reactions of ﬁve groups of bacterial type III PKSs. (A) RppA catalyzes the formation of THN which can
be oxidized by air or a dedicated oxygenase to yield ﬂaviolin. (B) PhlD constructs a phloroglucinol product from three units of
malonyl-CoA. (C) DpgA synthesizes DPA-CoA from four molecules of malonyl-CoA. (D) 1. ArsB utilizes three units of malonyl-
CoA to generate alkylresorcinols. 2. SrsA catalyzes the synthesis of alkylresorcinols with CoA esters of branched chain fatty acids
as starter substrates and both methylmalonyl-CoA and malonyl-CoA as the extender substrates. (E) 1. Gcs uses both CoA- and
ACP-tethered starters to assemble germicidin. 2. ArsC synthesizes triketide and tetraketide pyrones from fatty acyl starters and mal-
onyl-CoA. 3. PKS18 uses long chain acyl-CoAs as the starter units to synthesize a-pyrones in vitro.

figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 6. Typical reactions catalyzed by ORAS. ORAS uses fatty acyl-CoA starters to synthesize various triketides, tetraketides,

figure_candidates.label: Figure 7
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 7. Pyrone biosynthesis by CsyA. It uses either fatty acyl-CoAs or fatty acyl-SNACs as the starter units and catalyzes the
formation of triketide and tetraketide pyrones with malonyl-CoA as the extender unit.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 8
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 8. Proposed biosynthesis of csypyrone B1. It was proposed to be biosynthesized by condensation of succinyl-CoA with
three units of acetyl/malonyl-CoA under the catalysis of CsyB.
